intro.title: Welcome to Guelmim — gateway to the Sahara
intro.p1: Guelmim sits in southern Morocco as a historic trading town on the edge of the Sahara routes. Long known for its camel market, it remains a practical stop between the Atlantic coast (Sidi Ifni, Plage Blanche) and the road toward Tan-Tan and the deeper south.
intro.p2: The town itself is low-key: a working centre, weekly livestock trade, and easy access to one of the country's longest beaches. Plan one or two nights if you want the market, a beach half-day and a rest before continuing south or looping back toward Tiznit.

camel_market.title: Camel market
camel_market.p1: Guelmim's camel market is the reason many travellers stop here. On market days the edge of town fills with traders, animals and the practical chaos of a southern livestock souk — more working trade than tourist show.
camel_market.p2: Check the local market day before you go (traditionally associated with weekends, but confirm on the ground). Go early, dress modestly, and ask before close-up photos of people or animals.
camel_market.tip: Morning is best. Combine with a short walk in the centre the same day.

centre.title: Town centre & souks
centre.p1: Guelmim's centre is a functional southern town rather than a polished medina circuit. Small shops, cafés and everyday souk streets give a sense of local life between longer road stages.
centre.p2: Use it for supplies, a simple meal and orientation before Plage Blanche or the road south.
centre.tip: Late afternoon light is pleasant for a short loop on foot.

plage_blanche.title: Plage Blanche
plage_blanche.p1: Plage Blanche, west of Guelmim, is a huge sweep of Atlantic sand — often cited among Morocco's longest beaches. It feels remote and open rather than built-up.
plage_blanche.p2: Reach it by grand taxi or private car. Facilities are limited; bring water and sun protection. Swimming depends on swell and local advice.
plage_blanche.tip: Best as a half-day or sunset stop. Avoid midday heat in summer.

asrir.title: Asrir oasis area
asrir.p1: Near Guelmim, the Asrir area offers palms and a softer village landscape — a contrast to the open beach and the market dust.
asrir.p2: A short excursion if you want greenery and a slower pace without leaving the region.
asrir.tip: Pair with the centre in the morning and the beach later, or the reverse.

mosque.title: Central mosque & square
mosque.p1: The central mosque and surrounding square act as a simple landmark for navigating Guelmim on foot.
mosque.p2: Useful meeting point and a place to watch ordinary town life rather than a ticketed monument.
mosque.tip: Start or end your centre walk here.

coast_road.title: Coast road toward Sidi Ifni
coast_road.p1: The road linking Guelmim toward Sidi Ifni and the north-west coast is part of the journey's appeal — Atlantic light, open land and a change of pace from inland desert routes.
coast_road.p2: Ideal if you are self-driving or chaining grands taxis between the camel town and the Art Deco coast.
coast_road.tip: Allow extra time for photos and slow traffic near towns.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Guelmim?
q1.answer: One night covers the centre and a market or beach half-day; two nights if you want Plage Blanche at a slower pace.

q2.question: When is the camel market?
q2.answer: It follows a local weekly rhythm — confirm the day when you arrive. Mornings are the most active.

q3.question: How do I get to Guelmim?
q3.answer: By road from Agadir via Tiznit (roughly 3.5–4.5 hours depending on stops). Grands taxis and buses serve the route; a car is flexible for Plage Blanche.

q4.question: Is Plage Blanche worth it?
q4.answer: Yes if you want open Atlantic space rather than a resort strip. Go prepared: limited facilities, strong sun, and check swimming conditions.
